Why watching cashflow is mission critical 0:00 – 0:33 Opening promise healthy on paper bankrupt in March one month too late four first steps Picture a company that looks healthy on paper. It has a product, a big deal on the way, and a team that works hard. And in March it is bankrupt. Not because the business was bad, but because the money arrived one month too late. Nobody had drawn the simple board that showed it coming. Today I will show you why sales has to start long before you need the revenue, and four first steps you can take. 0:33 – 0:56 Who this is for founders founding team business or engineering later is expensive This is for founders and founding-team members. Maybe you are the business person, maybe you are the engineer. Either way you know you should sell. You just think it is something for later, once the product is ready. By the end I want you to see why later is the expensive answer.

Watch your cashflow 0:00 – 0:26 The board sticky notes January to April cash cost revenue costs every month Here is a board of sticky notes. One column for each month, January to April. Three rows: cash, cost and revenue. Start with the cost row. A cost note sits in every single column. Salaries, tools, rent. They do not wait for you. People still need paying on the last day of the month, whether or not a customer said yes. 0:26 – 1:02 Big deal lands in April big deal in April zero in March bankrupt a verbal yes is not cash Now the revenue row. There is one big note, and it sits in April. It is a good deal, a real one. But watch the cash row. Month by month the cash note gets smaller. In March it falls to zero dollars, and a stamp lands on it. Bankrupt. One month before the money would have arrived. A deal that is nearly done is not cash. A verbal yes is not cash either. Until the money is on the account, it does not count. 1:02 – 1:51 Find your zero-cash month first action your own board zero-cash month deadline for sales results count back So here is your first action. Build this board for your own company. Month by month: cash, cost and revenue, as simple as sticky notes. Then walk along the cash row and find the month where it reaches zero. That is your zero-cash month, and everything else today is measured against it. Pen and paper is enough, and twelve months is plenty. Be honest about the costs. Be careful with the revenue, and write only the revenue you would bet your own salary on. Write that date down. It is the deadline for your sales results, not for your product. Count back from it, and you know how much time you really have to start.

Why sales is more than just selling 0:00 – 0:20 Second reason cash is the first reason pays back before revenue insight process trust Cash is the first reason to start early. There is a second one, and it pays you back before a single dollar of revenue shows up. Selling early is not only about the money it brings in. It gives you three things: insight, a process, and trust.

Sales is more than selling 0:00 – 0:21 Insight every call replaces an assumption change or kill a feature first calls as research write down every surprise The first is insight. Every call replaces one assumption with something you actually heard. Maybe the first real conversation changes a feature, or kills one. That is cheaper than building the wrong thing for another three months. So treat the first calls as research. Write down every surprise. 0:21 – 0:58 Process close early deals yourself who buys why how long after ten deals a pattern no software needed The second is process. When you close early deals yourself, you see who buys, why they buy, and how long it takes. Write that down and repeat it. That is the beginning of a sales process. At first every deal is a surprise. After ten deals you may start to see a pattern: the same questions, the same worries, the same step where people go quiet. You do not need software for this. A page with the questions you asked and the answers you got is enough. 0:58 – 1:16 Trust letter of intent pipeline with real names you can win buyers buyers feel safer The third is trust. Early results such as a letter of intent, or a pipeline with real names in it, show that you can win buyers. A buyer who sees that others are talking to you feels safer talking to you as well. 1:16 – 1:38 All three build trust insight process and results same place buyers and investors trust you before the first dollar a good trade Put the three together. Insight, process and results all point to the same place. Buyers and investors get a reason to trust you. You can build that before your first dollar of revenue. It costs time and a bit of courage. That is why starting early is such a good trade.

How to start doing sales 0:00 – 0:17 From idea to practice how to start stages of a sale deal board marketing revenue pulled forward So how do you actually start? Three things. The stages a sale goes through, what a real deal board looks like, and where marketing fits in. After that we come back to our sticky-note board, with the revenue pulled forward.

Stages of sale 0:00 – 0:27 Three stages leads opportunities closing stranger to customer three words A sale has three stages, from left to right. Leads, opportunities, and closing. Each one is a different kind of work. Someone is a stranger, then a name on your list, then a conversation, then a customer. The stages are only names for where a person is on that way. Keep these three words, because the rest of this part uses them. 0:27 – 1:04 Leads second action spreadsheet ten names today every week company person why they care Start with leads. A lead is simply the name of someone who might buy. Research them and keep a list. This is your second action, and you can do it today. Open a spreadsheet, add ten names, and keep adding them every week. Do not make the list perfect. Write down the company, the person, and why you think they might care. If you do not know yet, write down a guess, and fix it after the first call. The only wrong list is the empty one. 1:04 – 1:37 First contact third action cold call inbound network short honest message a no teaches for free Then comes first contact. You can cold call, you can answer someone who came to you, or you can ask your network. Pick the one you are least afraid of and begin. This is your third action. Each conversation that goes somewhere turns a lead into an opportunity. Many people fear that they are bothering others. A short, honest message is a fair thing to send. And if they say no, you have learned something for free. 1:37 – 2:06 Opportunities the real work conversations questions proposal most of your week steady lead research Opportunities are where the real work lives. Conversations, questions, a proposal. If you spend all your time on lead research, you are researching, not selling. At some point a name has to become a conversation, and a conversation has to become a proposal. Put most of your week into the opportunities you already have. Keep a small, steady part for adding new names to the lead stage. 2:06 – 2:36 After closing signature delivery more waiting revenue after signature zero-cash month earlier Closing is not the end of the story for your cash. After the signature comes the delivery, and delivery is more waiting. Your revenue lands later than your signature, so count that gap into your board. How long does delivery take in your business? A week? A quarter? Add it to the board as a note after the signature, and you will find your zero-cash month a little earlier than you thought.

Pipeline tools in practice 0:00 – 0:30 Simple board one column per stage one card per deal count and value Monday morning who to call A deal board is simple. One column for each stage: New, Meeting, Proposal and Won. Each deal is one card. On top of each column you see how many deals sit there and what they are worth together. Imagine a Monday morning with this board in front of you. Two deals are in Proposal and one is stuck in Meeting. You know exactly who to call, and in which order. 0:30 – 1:07 Track every deal one step at a time nothing in your head stuck column empty column a minute not a quarter Then you track every deal. A card moves one step at a time, from one column to the next. Nothing lives only in your head, and nothing gets forgotten. This is also how you find problems. A column that fills up and never empties tells you where deals get stuck. A column that stays empty tells you where you have no flow. You cannot see either from your inbox. When something is stuck, you see it in a minute instead of finding out in a quarter. 1:07 – 1:30 Start simple no perfect tool spreadsheet sticky notes weekly habit fifteen minutes small and regular Do not wait for the perfect tool. A spreadsheet works. Sticky notes on a wall work. The tool matters much less than the habit of updating it every week. Pick a weekly slot, fifteen minutes. Move the cards, add the new ones, remove the dead ones. Small and regular beats big and rare.

How marketing feeds the pipeline 0:00 – 0:19 Marketing adds volume clear job more leads one stage first column the stage must exist Marketing has a clear job in this picture. It adds volume. It brings more leads into one stage of your pipeline, the first column of the board. A bigger flow of leads helps only if that stage exists and you know where it sits. 0:19 – 1:01 Defined entry point decide the stage measure it webinar or post forty new names compare on one board That only works if you decide which stage marketing feeds. If you do not, the volume goes in somewhere, but nobody can see where it goes or what it turns into. Give it a defined entry point, and then you can measure it. For example, a webinar or a post might bring in forty new names. If they all land in one column, you can see in a month how many of them became meetings. If they land nowhere, you have forty names and no idea. Marketing and your own outreach can then be compared on the same board. 1:01 – 1:23 Not a substitute do not wait for marketing your own first contact first opportunities do both carry the message But do not wait for marketing to do your first sales for you. Early on, your own first contact is what opens the first opportunities. Marketing helps it grow. So do both. Make the first calls yourself, learn what works, and then let marketing carry that message to many more people.

Watch your cashflow, revenue pulled in 0:00 – 0:12 Same board the board again same costs same four months one note different Here is the board again, with the same costs and the same four months. Only one note is different. That one note is what this whole talk is about. 0:12 – 0:39 Revenue earlier April revenue now in February cash dips but never zero stamp gone timing matters The April revenue note has moved. It now sits in February. Follow the cash row. It dips, but it never reaches zero. The stamp is gone, and the company lives on into the summer. In the first board you were out of money while waiting for a good deal. Here the same deal came earlier. That is how much timing matters. 0:39 – 0:57 How it moves not by hoping not a nicer spreadsheet start the pipeline earlier signed and paid in time How did the note move? Not by hoping, and not by a nicer spreadsheet. The only way is to start the pipeline earlier, so that the deal is signed and the money has arrived by the time the cost notes pile up.

Start before you need the money 0:00 – 0:17 Landing it one board left one question when do you start decided by what you start now We are almost there. One board is left, and it asks one question. When do you start? Everything so far was one idea, told on one board: the money you need later is decided by what you start now.

Watch your cashflow, "Start when?" 0:00 – 0:24 Revenue lags costs costs come first revenue months later already too late third time on the board Remember what the board told us. Costs come first. Revenue comes months later. And by the time you feel that you need sales, it is already too late. The first time you saw the problem. The second time you saw what changes if revenue comes sooner. This time you see what you do about it. 0:24 – 0:48 Start now start the pipeline now revenue before the cash runs out start when a few hours each week So start now. Start the pipeline before you need the money, so that the revenue lands before the cash runs out. The board points back to the first quarter and asks, start when? None of this needs a big budget or a new hire. It needs a few hours of your attention each week, starting now. 0:48 – 1:09 Four steps zero-cash month list of potential customers first contact deal board conversion rate and cycle Here are the four steps once more. First, build your cashflow view and find your zero-cash month. Second, start a list of potential customers. Third, make first contact. Fourth, put your deals on a board and measure your conversion rate and cycle. None of them needs permission from anyone. 1:09 – 1:38 This week pick one step start this week put it in your calendar small version first Do not try to do all four at once. Pick one step, the one that scares you least, and start it this week. Put it in your calendar now, with a time and a place. When you meet your cashflow board next month, you will be glad you did. Do the small version first. Ten minutes on the board is better than a perfect plan that starts next quarter.
